title: The Long Glide
tagline: Out of fuel at 10,500 ft — Lydd is 22 miles away.
history: Inspired by airliners that ran out of fuel in flight — after a fuel-quantity mix-up in 1983, after an unnoticed leak in 2001 — and were glided to a landing: one on a disused air base, one on an island runway.
situation: 10,500 ft over the Channel inbound to Lydd at first light, 170 aboard. A leak nobody noticed has drained the tanks: the engines are about to flame out. The runway is 1,505 m long and you will have one go at it.
failures: Fuel exhausted: both engines flame out, the APU has no fuel
Ram-air turbine: blue hydraulics and essential electrics only
Gear by gravity (alternate extension); brakes on the accumulator
tips: Best glide is about 210 kt clean — you have more height than distance, so manage the excess
Speed brakes and a wide S-turn to lose height; lower the gear late (it's draggy)
Gravity gear: O → Systems → ALT GEAR
Aim for the threshold — there is no go-around

do.note: F/O: Fuel imbalance… no — fuel's gone. Both tanks. We're going to lose them.
ATC: Lydd runway 03 is yours, 22 miles, wind calm. Emergency services alerted.

objectives.text: Land and stop on the runway
